title: .opt-out-from-anonymous-statistics still leaks referrer
body:
<!---
When creating a bug report please:
- Verify first that your issue is not already reported on GitHub
- Test if the latest release and master branch are affected too.
- Provide a clear and concise description of what the bug is in "Bug report 
  summary" section.
- Try to provide as much information about your environment (OS distribution,
  running in container, etc.) as possible to allow us reproduce this bug faster.
- Write which component is affected. We group our components the same way our
  code is structured so basically:
  component name = dir in top level directory of repository
- Describe how you found this bug and how we can reproduce it. Preferable with
  a minimal test-case scenario. You can paste gist.github.com links for larger
  files
- Provide a clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
-->

##### Bug report summary
Creating the file `.opt-out-from-anonymous-statistics ` to opt-out telemetry seems to have no effect.

I have put the file in `/opt/netdata/etc/netdata/.opt-out-from-anonymous-statistics`, `/etc/netdata/.opt-out-from-anonymous-statistics`

I tried to write `all` in the file as specified in a documentation I read but I cannot find anymore.
File is permissioned to netdata user.

I am aware of the documentation here: https://docs.netdata.cloud/docs/anonymous-statistics/ 

Whatever I do, i see the call to `https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?` 

Additionally, i'd like to report it here for telemetry as well, I also see a call to `https://netdata.cloud/account/sso-agent`, which is not expected as I already run I run my own registry to avoid calls to my-netdata.io

##### OS / Environment
CoreOS Stable

##### Netdata version (ouput of `netdata -V`)
v1.12.1

##### Component Name
netdata 

##### Steps To Reproduce
Install netdata 1.12.1 with release page run.gz on CoreOs Stable, try to disable telemetry as per documentation

##### Expected behavior
I expect netdata to respect my configuration options
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
What you see has to do with how Google Tag Manager works. As described in https://docs.netdata.cloud/docs/anonymous-statistics/#google-tag-manager
> We have configured GTM to trigger the tag only when the variable anonymous_statistics is true. The value of this variable is controlled via the opt-out mechanism.

You may see a call to GTM when you have the file, but nothing is sent to Google analytics. There are many ways to see what GTM does exactly and when it triggers tags. A quick search brought up the following:

https://www.analyticsmania.com/post/how-to-check-if-google-tag-manager-is-working/

> I tried to write all in the file as specified in a documentation I read but I cannot find anymore.

You don't need to write anything on the file, just `touch` it. We found this much more user-friendly.

> Additionally, i'd like to report it here for telemetry as well, I also see a call to https://netdata.cloud/account/sso-agent, which is not expected as I already run I run my own registry to avoid calls to my-netdata.io

This has nothing to do with telemetry. The call is for the sign-in functionality only. It sends no information other than the referrer, which can't be avoided.

As for the relationship with the local registry: We are building a lot of features that can only be provided via proper authentication/authorization and a centralized control system (on the cloud or on premise), so signing in will soon be much more than just seeing the servers you have visited.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
You may be able to stop the referrer from leaking by injecting the following headers on the HTTP responses from the Netdata nodes:

```
Content-Security-Policy: referrer same-origin
Referrer-Policy: same-origin
```

Assuming your browser follows those correctly, that will prevent it from sending any `Referer` header at all when making requests from the Netdata dashboard or navigating away from it.  I'm not sure if we are explicitly setting a `Referer` header though when we send such requests, and the above solution probably won't stop that if we are.

We haven't found a way to prevent loading `gtm.js` when statistics are enabled. As you'll see [here](https://docs.netdata.cloud/docs/anonymous-statistics/#google-tag-manager), we state that

> The only thing that’s impossible for us to prevent from being sent is the URL in the “Referrer” Header of the browser request to GA. However, the settings above ensure that all stored URLs and host names are anonymized

If you, or anyone else can help us find a with a way to prevent this from happening when telemetry is disabled, we'll be happy to merge such a PR.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
As mentioned above, setting a referrer policy should do this for most people (of the major browsers, only IE, Edge, and stuff on iOS ignores this).  The two options for this are either:

* The HTTP `Referrer-Policy` header (and yes, that is spelled correctly).  This may cause issues for some users who are proxying things.
* A `<meta name='referrer' />` tag in the HTML.  This one isn't as universally handled by some browsers, and may still leak referrer information if it comes after any tags that load external resources.

In either case, the value needs to be `same-origin`, which will prevent sending a `Referer` header to other origins, but continue to send one for the origin the Netdata dashboard is hosted on (which may be important for security reasons).  I can confirm that the header approach works, as I've got that set on all the nginx instances I proxy Netdata through, and see no `Referer` header in the requests for GTM.

[More info on MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Referrer-Policy)

comments.body:
@cakrit 

> We haven't found a way to prevent loading `gtm.js` when statistics are enabled. As you'll see [here](https://docs.netdata.cloud/docs/anonymous-statistics/#google-tag-manager), we state that.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
> you mean **when statistics are enabled** or **when statistics are disabled**? Maybe I got something wrong, I just want to clarify this.

Yes, you got it wrong. See https://docs.netdata.cloud/docs/anonymous-statistics/#opt-out:
*- The Google Tag Manager Javascript snippet will remain in the page, but the linked tag will not be fired. The effect is that no data will ever be sent to GA.*

> Searching for `gtm.js` in this repository shows me, that `goto-host-from-alarm.html` and `console.html` does not check for the opt out flag. Is this behavior intended?

No GTM tags are triggered from `goto-host-from-alarm.html`. If we ever add a tag for it, we'll put the condition in. 

`console.html` access requires creating an account and signing in first. Our [privacy policy](http://netdata.cloud/legal/privacy-policy) explains everything we collect and how we use it. See section 3 especially. We mention there the following:

> Website and Analytics: When you visit our Websites and use our Services, ND collects some information about your activities through tools such as Google Analytics. The type of information that we collect focuses on general information such as country or city where you are located, pages visited, time spent on pages, heat-map of visitors’ activity on the site, information about the browser you are using, etc. ND collects and uses this information pursuant to our legitimate interest in enhancing the security and utility of our Services. The information we gather and process is used in the aggregate to spot trends without deliberately identifying individuals.

> Note that you can learn about Google’s practices in connection with its analytics services and how to opt out of it by downloading the Google Analytics opt-out browser add-on, available at https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout.

Please note that the intent of the `.opt-out-from-anonymous-statistics` flag was to completely disable sending the host information described in that policy and in https://docs.netdata.cloud/docs/anonymous-statistics/. That information is quite different than anything that any pageview/session info GA collects. Of course we're happy to investigate all suggestions. 

As always, we're completely transparent about what we do and why we do it.  You do realize of course that we don't want to make all data collection opt-in, because we'd be completely blind. But let's continue this discussion and we'll do more things and update the privacy policy if that's what makes sense.

*P.S. I haven't been able to do the referrer test I mentioned yet, I hope I can get to it today*

comments.body:
@c33s hi, I just wanted to give you a little update. We are actually working on moving from GA and GTM for the agent to a self hosted PostHog instance. Idea being we can finally get off Google for the agent side and PostHog will actually enable much better product insights anyway to keep trying to make improvements. So no data going to Google for the open source agent analytics is the aim here and actually owning and protecting the analytics data we depend on to help spot issues earlier and understand the product usage to better see how to keep improving it. 

PostHog is open source and pretty well tuned in to privacy concerns. Check them out https://posthog.com/docs#philosophy

We are testing this on our demo servers at the moment so hopefully within the next release or two we will be swapping out PostHog for GA. 

Happy to chat more about this with you if you'd like and share the details.

still there are two important points for me (while the first makes the 2nd obsolete)
- it must be opt-in 
- if the user doesn't opt-in or opted-out, tracking must be completely disabled. no exceptions

all this "we only track a bit" or "we track to our servers" or "we anonymize this or that part" is not ok, opt-out or not-opt-in means **no tracking at all; full stop**.

anonymizing simply does not work ([Robust De-anonymization of Large Sparse Datasets][1], [So wenig nützt Daten-Anonymisierung ][2] (german). nearly every time you have "anonymized" data, you can reconnect the data to a person with 3-5 control/connection points.

GDPR is about personal information and we have none of that. Regardless of what the paper says, we have no information at our disposal regarding FOSS agent users, unless someone chooses to sign-in to the cloud and provide us with an email address. GTM can't even track a user across different agent UIs, as each has a separate URL, that is unknown to us. 

For anyone still concerned, disabling anonymous statistics and setting up a private registry are both very well documented and quite easy to configure. We can't even know how many users use netdata, because of these opt-out methods.

comments.author: Participant 10
comments.body:
One workaround for software that disregards user consent like this is to use a browser plugin like uBlock Origin, and blacklist all of the domains (such as GTM, GA, netdata.cloud, et c) that they try to talk to.  This won't help for other users of the web UI, but if it's just you accessing your own servers, this will prevent the HTML client from phoning home from any browser so configured.

It's a stupid hack and shouldn't be necessary, but is often faster than fighting with developers of web apps that feel somehow entitled to user data.
